subject: Random effects in the prediction stack

messages.author: 048d1222bb0af667
messages.subject: Random effects in the prediction stack
parts:
Hello everyone!

I have made a huge progress in my code and in using INLA since my last question here but now I have a question I would like to discuss with you because I don't really know what R is doing behind the code I wrote.

I built a stack for estimation with my spatial data, 2 covariates, the spatial effect and one random effect and then I built the prediction stack only with NA data, the same 2 covariates and the spatial effect because I'm not interested in using the random effects for prediction. However, honestly, I don't know what is the code actually running and I don't understand how is R not complaining about not having the random effect.

In another question here in the group I found that I could give the prediction stack a new level of the random effect: for exemple, my random effects go from level 1 to 24 and I associated the level 25 as a random effect in the prediciton stack. The thing is that I have results when I don't give any random effect and when I do, so I know something is going on behind the code but I can't justify or understand what is the right thing to do.

I appreciate any comments  and help you can give me on this subject!

Hope to year from you soon :)
Ema Biscaia

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Random effects in the prediction stack
parts:
Hello, Elias

Thank you for your time helping me!

I saw the example and I don't think it has random efects like the ones I'm using in my project.
My problem is that the model gives different predictions when I write the stack for predition with and without random effects.

The code for the stacks I use in my model is like this:

stk.estimation <- inla.stack(tag = "est",
  data = list(y = binary.data, numtrials = 1),
  A = list(1,A,1),
  effects = list(data.frame(cov1 = covariate1 , cov2=covariate2),
                 s = indexs, lvl =random.effect))
 
stk.prediction <- inla.stack(tag = "pred",
  data = list(y = NA, numtrials = NA),
  A = list(1, Ap,1),
  effects = list(data.frame(cov1 = dp[, 4],cov2 = dp[, 5]),
                 s = indexs ))

For the prediction data I'm not interested in giving the levels of the random effects because I actually don't have them. I just want to use the random efects "lvl" to adjust the model but I don't know if the model sees them only for that purpose or what is it doing when I don't write any random effects in the prediction data.

Thank you again for your attention!
Ema Biscaia

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Random effects in the prediction stack
parts:
I am not sure if I understood your point. If you don't include it in
the data stack it will not be in the corresponding linear predictor
and the predictions _will_ actually be different as expected.
